title: Windbreaker Shorts Are Having A Moment — These Are The Best
text:
Windbreaker Shorts Are Having A Moment — These Are The Best
The revival of windbreaker shorts was not on my 2026 bingo card, but alas, they’ve become a pillar of athleisure. First popularized in the ’80s and ’90s, the lightweight, swishy bottoms were known for bold, color-blocked designs reserved for the gym. Still, it wasn’t long before style icons like the Sex and the City character Carrie Bradshaw pushed the boundaries, wearing the silhouette with kitten heels and a crop top.

A similar reinvention is unfolding now, with It girls putting a fashion-forward spin on the nostalgic briefs, which take their name from their jacket counterpart. Oversized T-shirts, designer handbags, sculpting corsets, and sleek flats are becoming a natural extension of sprinter shorts — and while you’re bound to spot an abundance of hot pants in the park, you'll also start finding them on city streets, in airports, and potentially at a casual happy hour.

"In general these shorts are part of a much broader movement where athletic pieces are being re-contextualized through unexpected styling, whether that's with tailoring, feminine separates, or vintage accessories. It's less about dressing for the game and more about borrowing the energy that sport represents," stylist and Depop trends spokesperson Gabriella Karefa-Johnson tells Refinery29.

It’s all about knowing how to style the retro shell cutoffs. For an undeniably casual look, reach for a simple tee, crew socks, and sneakers. It delivers an unfussy gym-to-street look that may just be the easiest entry point into the trend. If you're aiming for a more elevated aesthetic, contrast is key. Slip into a slinky lace tank and add a structured layer, like an asymmetrical blazer or cinched trench coat. The interplay between sporty nylon and chic tailoring is where the magic happens. 

Unexpected footwear is yet another clever style direction. The shorts feel more intentional when paired with minimalist sandals, ballet flats, and pumps. It’s a simple way to upgrade the piece without overthinking the entire look — turning a sporty staple into a fashion-forward moment.

title: The Under-The-Radar Summer Accessory That Makes Every Outfit Pop
text:
The Under-The-Radar Summer Accessory That Makes Every Outfit Pop
With summer in full swing, it’s only right that we’ve swapped our shoe rotation for sandals, flats, and retro sneakers. With that comes the opportunity to show off a special piece of jewelry: anklets. For many, these are a staple that never went “away,” but it’s still worth calling out that the anklets trending today are not like the ones we grew up with.

Today’s coolest anklets translate the whimsy and love for color we’re seeing across fashion into candy above the feet. They have a touch of fancy, brought forth by bright gems, charms, and layered metals. We’ve noticed them cropping up throughout the fashion world, on runways here and there, but mostly in street style and on celebrities like Rihanna, Hailey Bieber, and Gigi Hadid. Rather than the dainty chains that have traditionally been popular, today’s anklets are bigger and more embellished. 

“Anklet stacks are huge right now,” Christin Marie Nichols, founder and CEO of Christin Marie Studio, adds. “Just like bracelets, customizing your anklet stack is a statement of self-expression that speaks to your individuality. What you choose to incorporate, how creative you can get, how many you use, [how you mix] mixed metals and materials… [these are] all factors that I love to see. Anklets are moving from being a minimal aesthetic touch to a bold show of character.”

Nichols’ own celebrity-worn jewelry brand is known for its maximalism, which extends to the brand’s array of anklets boasting sizable and multichromatic gemstones. “The combination of colors I use are made to complement anything you wear and are so eye-catching. It’s almost like organized chaos but pretty. With it being so unique it attracts attention where people normally wouldn’t pay attention,” the founder adds.

Ahead, shop our 11 favorite anklets, including gold options, minimalist picks, and what maximalist dreams are made of. Several options ahead work year-round, and some others are especially good for wearing during the warmer months and on tropical vacations.

title: A Week In Washington, D.C. On A $72,977 Salary
text:
A Week In Washington, D.C. On A $72,977 Salary

Welcome to Money Diaries where we are tackling the ever-present taboo that is money. We’re asking real people how they spend their hard-earned money during a seven-day period — and we’re tracking every last dollar.

This week: a fundraising writer working in the arts who makes $72,977 per year and spends some of it on margaritas.

If you’d like to submit your own Money Diary, you can do so via our online form. We pay $150 for each published diary. Apologies but we’re not able to reply to every email. We are legally unable to publish any diaries that have been written with the use of AI.

This diary was written in 2026.

Interested in taking our latest Money Diaries survey? We’d love to hear your thoughts here.

Occupation: Fundraising writer
Industry: Arts and culture
Age: 25
Location: Washington, D.C.
Salary: $72,977
Joint Income/Financial Setup:
Assets:
High yield savings account: $8,270
Health savings account: $1,000
Brokerage account: $7,295 ($2,200 is not invested in any stocks as I keep it liquid for everyday spending and big purchases)
Employer-sponsored tax-deferred annuity plan: $11,050
Rollover IRA from high school and college jobs: $4,945
Checking and savings at a credit union: $100
Unmatured savings bonds: ~$20,000
Debt: $9,590 for a car loan and $4,760 on my credit card balance
Paycheck Amount (Biweekly): $1,999.95
Pronouns: She/her

Monthly Expenses

Housing Costs: $1,305 for my portion of rent (I live with two roommates in a two-story row house).
Loan Payments: $400 (car loan payments)
Utilities: ~$100-$200 for gas, electricity, and wifi (a third of an equal split that varies month to month).
Health, vision, & dental: $350 for Invisalign (last payment will be made in January, 2027); $16 for dental and vision post-tax. I’m on my parents’ health insurance plan.
Phone: $30 (I got a new iPhone last year, so I send this to my mom when I remember).
Credit card: $400
Subscriptions: $88 for the gym, $10 for Microsoft (I don’t know how to cancel this), $12.99 for AppleTV, $6 for NYT, and $9 for Patreon. My parents pay for all of the other streaming services I use.
Savings: $700 goes to my brokerage account and $450 goes to my HYSA.

Was there an expectation for you to attend higher education? Did you participate in any form of higher education? If yes, how did you pay for it?
It was an unspoken expectation that I would attend college, especially since we are Black. My parents paid for tuition, my books, and my room and board (eventually my rent and a car, too, once I moved off-campus). I worked four jobs at a time during my undergrad for discretionary spending on utilities, clothes, travel, etc. I’m being pushed to get a Master’s degree or terminal degree. Both my parents have Master’s degrees and Master’s certificates. Everyone in my family — my grandparents, my aunts, my uncles, and my cousins — all have multiple degrees. I would like to get my Master’s, and I even recently got accepted into a couple of grad schools, but the cost (even after sizeable scholarships) was too expensive to seriously consider going at this point in my life.

Growing up, what kind of conversations did you have about money? Did your parent(s) educate you about finances?
We didn’t really speak about money until I got my first job. My mom handles the finances for the family since my dad has a habit of overpaying bills. She taught me two things: (1) even if you only put away a dollar, you’ll have a dollar to go back to later; (2) I’ve spent more on less. The latter statement has been a devastating piece of advice that has guided me through some dumb financial decisions in my early twenties.

What was your first job and why did you get it?
My first job was in the eleventh grade. I earned around $10 an hour to run lights and sound for rented events in my high school auditorium. I originally got the job because I had a crush on this boy and I wanted to spend more time with him. He kind of set me up, though, because I’d work all the events he didn’t want to. After he graduated, I started working regularly with a church that rented the auditorium every Sunday. Through this job, I set up my first retirement account.

Did you worry about money growing up?
Never. I had a very nice childhood. My parents were frugal. Once a year, we’d go to Disney World, Las Vegas, the Bahamas, or somewhere of the sort. However, when my younger sister and I started playing travel sports, we started traveling almost every week from March through November. For a long time, I thought my parents had secretly won the lottery because there was suddenly money for everything.

Do you worry about money now?
Not really. I should be. I don’t budget at all. As my mother says: What is money if not something to be spent? I hover between $4,000-$5,000 in CC debt that could be paid off. I could ask my parents for help, but they’ve already paid $3,000 off once before, after I finished undergrad. I’m reticent about revealing I’ve racked that balance back up.

At what age did you become financially responsible for yourself and do you have a financial safety net?
I’m not completely financially responsible for myself. My parents pay for a lot: my health insurance, my phone service, my car insurance, my EZ pass, vacations, and sometimes even my groceries. I’m very fortunate and grateful for their support. It goes without saying but they are my safety net.

Do you or have you ever received passive or inherited income? If yes, please explain.
Yes, my parents send me around $160 monthly. My dad sends $60 to a checking account, and my mom sends $100 to my brokerage account. When I was in college, they used to send me around ~$500 a month on top of the money they’d send me for rent. Additionally, I have around $20,000 of unmatured savings bonds that my parents set up for me. I’ve spent around $4,500 in unmatured bonds so far. My parents let my sister and me know that in case they don’t live forever, we will share a trust that will include all their assets.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day One: Monday

7:15 a.m. — Every weekday, my Alexa is scheduled to turn on the lights and tell me the weather to wake me up. I try not to ignore her today. After getting ready, I grab my pre-packed lunch and make my coffee then leave with one of my roommates.

8:15 a.m. — We hop on the Metro. It’s subsidized by my organization, so I don’t pay fares. $2.50 (Expensed)

10:00 a.m. — Lately, I’ve been in a holding pattern. I’ll work on something, then wait two weeks for review and approval. There’s not much else to do other than read the news and play NYT games. Occasionally, I’ll go on a deep dive of a wealthy donor and wonder why I didn’t decide to pursue a career as a generous heiress, a specialized doctor, or a corporate lawyer.

12:00 p.m. — I’m meeting a friend for lunch. I brought my meal, but I need something to drink and a little snack. $5.65

5:00 p.m. — I take the Metro back home, get changed, and head to the gym. $2.50 (Expensed)

6:30 p.m. — After my weight-lifting class, I buy a few snacks and a bottle of wine. This week, I’m hosting my friends for our weekly get-together. Sometimes my roommates join us. $15.31

8:00 p.m. — My friends arrive and we chat about our week as some terrible dating show plays in the background.

11:45 p.m. — My friends leave and the day is done. I say nighty-night to the poos (my roommates), then take a shower and scroll on my phone for a bit.

Daily Total: $20.96

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day Two: Tuesday

7:45 a.m. — I finally drag myself out of bed. I put myself together fairly quickly, but I can’t find my blazer. I waste quite a bit of time looking for it. There’s no time to make coffee. So, I grab my lunch in the form of my leftover pasta dinner and head out. My roommate concedes she will also be late to work. I bid her farewell and walk past three coffee shops on my way to the Metro. $2.50 (Expensed)

9:30 a.m. — There’s an organization-wide meeting. Everyone is so neurotic…too many PhDs per capita. Ever since my organization cancelled remote working, people have been cranky. I won’t lie, I don’t enjoy coming in every day.

10:45 a.m. — My landlord has scheduled a new dryer to be installed at 12 p.m. and let us know at the last minute. I’ll have to leave work and jump on the Metro. $2.25 (Expensed)

1:15 p.m. — Today has been a comedy of errors. The dryer is too big. I try to call my landlord and get no answer. I do get in touch with an incredulous colleague of hers, and she tells me to tell the men to take back the dryer they have already plugged in and hooked up. After I get off the phone, the men say they can’t take it back because it’s already hooked up. AHHHHHHHH! I just wanna wash my clothes, bro. I just sign the little delivery thing and let them haul away the old dryer. I take a picture of the too-big dryer for my landlord and haul my ass back to the Metro. $2.25 (Expensed)

1:45 p.m. — The landlord calls me. She had a feeling it wouldn’t fit. :/ Gorl, you must be joking. She needs us to take measurements of the dryer and the space it needs to fit in. She’s a nice lady, but she’s putting me through it.

4:45 p.m. — It’s time to depart. Despite the cancellation of remote working, I’m able to convince my manager to let me work from home the next two days before I leave for my weekend trip to Pittsburgh, so I’m done with running around for a while. $2.50 (Expensed)

6:00 p.m. — I cook a mediocre meal of sauteed peppers and breaded cod. After dinner, I decide to head upstairs as I remember that I owe my landlord the dryer measurements. I call my mom to vent about the situation. She’s of the mindset that I should tell my landlord that the washer is also broken so she’ll replace them both. I want to but I just can’t bring myself to do that. I’ll wait until the washer actually breaks.

12:30 a.m. — A shower and a sing-along later. I head to bed to scroll for a few hours.

Daily Total: $0

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day Three: Wednesday

7:15 a.m. — My alarm goes off. The lights come on. I turn over to ignore it all. After 30 minutes or so, I head downstairs to set up my coffee. One of my roommates is also working from home. WiFi is spotty upstairs and the only places to sit are the living room or the kitchen bar. She’s already parked in the living room, so I take the bar.

12:30 p.m. — Whoa, I had back-to-back meetings this morning. My roommate didn’t feel like cooking lunch and asked if I wanted to explore local dining. So we ordered some Thai food to pick up. One Panang curry for me. $22

3:30 p.m. — It’s a marathon of meetings today. I had to eat my lunch around several of them. This job is so interesting. Sometimes there’s absolutely nothing to do and other times it seems like you’re planning the five-year trajectory of the state of the world.

6:00 p.m. — I finally drag myself from work and run to the gym for my 6:15 p.m. Body Pump class. During my class, one of my roommates texts saying they found a nicer dining table set on Facebook Marketplace. Our dining room is in desperate need of some real seating. Split between the three of us, the price isn’t too bad for a long table and six chairs. My parents volunteer to come help us collect it tomorrow. They’re so sweet.

7:30 p.m. — I get back home and reheat my leftover curry. My roommates and I end up watching this terrible TV show, Sirens. One of my roommates suggests finishing the entire show. I agree. I’m comfortable, we’re chatting, and I do have a glass of wine in my hand.

11:15 p.m. — I head upstairs for a shower and another couple hours of scrolling on my phone.

Daily Total: $22

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day Four: Thursday

7:15 a.m. — Alexa has done her job again. I’m thinking about where I want to go this summer. The beach, definitely. Maybe I can squeeze a weekend trip somewhere out of $500?

8:30 a.m. — I’m working from home again. I’m typing away on my computer, and I’m starting to need some coffee. I forgot that I’m leaving for my trip tomorrow! I need to start packing. I throw all the underwear I can find in my suitcase.

11:00 a.m. — My first meeting of the day and we’re already talking in circles. My poor supervisor is trying to explain an approval process for a waiver and the other team lead is just not getting it. It’s like pulling teeth.

12:00 p.m. — Another meeting, I decide to go camera off since it’s a larger one. I go back to slowly packing while the meeting continues. I’d love to wash a batch of clothes, but they’d have to air dry before 12 p.m. tomorrow and I only have so many places I can hang my clothes.

1:15 p.m. — The men from Home Depot arrive to pick up the too-big dryer. A replacement is supposed to come tomorrow. I pray that it’s the right size.

5:15 p.m. — The computer is finally closed, and my suitcase is open as I try to make sure I’ll have everything I’ll need. I run to the store for some snacks for the trip. We’re driving four hours to Pittsburgh, but my friend doesn’t like to stop. I hope a five-pound bag of Swedish Fish and a case of sparkling water will see me through the weekend. $18.23

8:00 p.m. — My dad arrives at my place. We wait at the house for a bit since the lady is running behind. Eventually, we get to the lady’s house. She and her husband are nice. They have the cutest dog too. It literally reminds me of a toddler. They’re moving to Spain to teach English and are trying to sell us other items in their house, but we only need the table. It was a little too big to fit through their front door, so we had to take it apart a little bit. Their house was a little bare. I pray they had a pair of pliers. Huzzah, they do! After we take everything away to our cars, we pay her for the table and chairs. Of course, I carried a third of the share. $84

9:00 p.m. — We make it back to the house. I hug my dad goodbye after he remained surprisingly patient with my lack of strength carrying the table. My roommates and I work out how to put the table back together and carry it to our dining room. After placing the chairs, we admire our find. It’s solid wood and a considerable steal for its quality. I’m glad we spent our money on a secondhand table rather than some cheap set from Wayfair.

11:45 p.m. — After watching TV for a bit, my roommates and I head upstairs.

Daily Total: $102.23

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day Five: Friday

7:15 a.m. — Today, the garbage men wake me up.

9:15 a.m. — My roommate asks if I want to get coffee and breakfast. I’m literally about to buy every meal for the next three days…I should save a little money and crack open the eggs on my shelf in the fridge. But I say sure, and fifteen minutes later, we are out the door. I drop way more than it was worth for a watered-down iced chai tea and a bacon, egg, and cheese bagel. $18.50

11:00 a.m. — We eat our overpriced breakfast at our brand new dining room table.

12:15 p.m. — My friends arrive to pick me up and we are off to Pittsburgh!

2:45 p.m. — We actually do make a stop. Everyone wants to eat. I’ve never been big on gas station food, but I make do with a BLT wrap and some chips. Also, my roommate texts me that the dryer is finally installed!! $9.09

5:15 p.m. — We arrive in Pittsburgh at our Airbnb. It’s gigantic. There are nine of us staying in it, so I have to share a bed with one of my friends, but I don’t mind.

8:45 p.m. — After heading to the store for liquor and mixers, we pregame for a bit before we head to a local gay bar to watch the finale of RuPaul’s Drag Race. $10.69

11:30 p.m. — We’re in a different gay bar and dancing the night away. My buzz is starting to die so I get another round of drinks. $7.45

1:45 a.m. — Eventually, we tire out and split an Uber back to the Airbnb. Split six ways, my share is only $5.12. Oddly enough, the other members of our group that didn’t go out are up and watching National Treasure when we arrive. After finishing the movie and brushing my teeth, I finally fall into bed. $5.12

Daily Total: $50.85

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day Six: Saturday

9:00 a.m. — I slowly wake up. My friends are chatting about what they want to do for the day. I’m very go-with-the-flow. The big event for me is the Pirates game tomorrow so I’m down to do whatever. After a shower, I head out with one of my friends to a local coffee place. I end up getting a pretty decent coffee and a pastry. However, the pastry is too sweet, and I didn’t have dinner last night, so I end up ordering a hearty breakfast sandwich. $21.12

11:00 a.m. — We meet up with other members of our group and a mutual friend who works at Pitt. She takes us on a brief walking tour of the campus. We end up at the Phipps Conservatory. $22.95

2:00 p.m. — After a lovely time, we’re all a little hungry and take the bus to a local dive. $2.75

3:30 p.m. — One Caesar salad later, we head back to the Airbnb. Luckily, the bus pass is valid for three hours, so we just hop back on. $14.75

7:30 p.m. — We head back out to do a larger group dinner with some local friends. The restaurant we’re at is this old church that’s been converted to a brewery. It’s sick. I end up splitting a large pasta dish with my friend. $22.33

9:00 p.m. — After dinner, we head to a local cash-only bar around the block to watch the end of the Penguins game. My friend spots me and buys me a beer.

11:15 p.m. — The home team loses so some of us decide to head to one of our local friend’s place for a nightcap. We catch a bus. $2.75

1:45 a.m. — After chit-chatting for a few hours, we call an Uber home and call it a night. We split the Uber four ways. $4.65

Daily Total: $91.30

DashDividers_1_500x100

Day Seven: Sunday

8:00 a.m. — We wake to find that it is 30 degrees outside. It was literally in the high 70s yesterday!!! I only have a sweatshirt and some thin yoga pants. I beg my friend to take us to a local thrift store before we sit in the cold for four hours.

10:30 a.m. — Six of us head out in two cars. I end up buying two books at one of the bookstores we stopped at. $33.22

10:45 a.m. — I find some cargo pants at a thrift store down the street. I immediately slip them on over my yoga pants. I’m not shivering as violently as I was before. $10

12:00 p.m. — We meet up with the rest of the group back at the Airbnb then head over to the baseball stadium. My friend drives around for 20 minutes trying to find somewhere to park. Finally, we crawl out of the car and walk about 15 minutes to the stadium.

1:00 p.m. — We finally get settled in our seats in the nosebleed section. It’s freezing, but we’re still determined to do our nine dogs, nine beers, nine innings game. It’s a hefty cost for two beers, chicken fingers, and cold fries. $44.74

4:15 p.m. — Pirates win! We’re supposed to go out to a bar later this evening but I’m not sure I have it in me. We head back to the Airbnb for a nap.

6:30 p.m. — I wake to find that everyone is still asleep. Eventually, we all wake up and game plan. The couples in the group will go out for dinner and the singletons will find something to do until we all meet up at the bar later. Two friends and I go to a ramen place for dinner. I’m not that hungry but I don’t want to feel left out so I order broth and some noodles. $11.74

9:00 p.m. — Everyone is feeling tired and our plans to meet up have fallen through. We’re not ready to call it a night yet so we meet up with one of the couples at a Mexican restaurant. It’s surprisingly good and has some interesting drinks. $18.45

10:00 p.m. — We share an Uber to get back home. Split five ways, it’s $5.77. We have a few more drinks and watch a movie. $5.77

11:45 p.m. — I try to pack up a bit because we’re leaving around nine in the morning. All in all, it was a super relaxing trip. It was good to visit friends. We talked about making this an annual trip that we do every year. Eventually, I do Venmo my friend who drove us from DC for gas (split four ways). $35.55

Daily Total: $159.47

DashDividers_1_500x100

The Breakdown

Conclusion:
I definitely spent way more this week than I usually do. I’m very big on cooking all my meals and making coffee. After recording my spending this week, I’ll definitely be more committed to meal prepping. I might even think about budgeting, but who knows?

title: This Travel-Ready Hoodie Is The Best Thing I’ve Bought All Year
text:
This Travel-Ready Hoodie Is The Best Thing I’ve Bought All Year

I can’t tell you how many social media ads I scroll past on any given day. However, I can tell you that the stars must have aligned (or fine, my algorithm reflected a love of naps, kittens, and other cozy things) to unite me with Comfrt, specifically the brand’s now internet-famous Airplane Mode Travel Hoodie.

When I tell you that a truer match couldn’t be conjured in heaven, I’m barely exaggerating. The moment I saw Comfrt’s hoodie with a built-in eye mask, my thumb and heart both stopped. The next thing I knew, I’d hit “place order” on matching sweatshirts for me and my husband.

That was back in February, and over five months later, the Comfrt Airplane Mode Travel Hoodie is still among my most-worn items in my closet. (In my mind, it’s more than paid for itself in terms of how many times I wear it.) But unique features aside, it’s a really well-made sweatshirt. It’s constructed from a sturdy yet soft cotton-polyester fabric that doesn’t look bulky. It’s become the first thing I pack when I’m going on a trip, and when I’m home? I wear it when I need a quick power nap and am asleep within minutes (according to my Oura ring). And if you’re out and about running errands, just tuck the eye mask into the hood or wear the hood as you would normally with any other hoodie. title: The Handbag Trend That Effortlessly Transitions From Summer To Fall
text:
The Handbag Trend That Effortlessly Transitions From Summer To Fall
Fashion is far from that post-pandemic dopamine dressing bubble, and it’s also emerging from a sweeping beige wave and quiet luxury spell. It’s certainly not dead, celebrity stylist Gabriella Karefa-Johnson tells Refinery29, “but the appetite for texture and pattern is definitely back, and snakeskin certainly has a starring role to play.” Fashion feels like it’s returning to a more whimsical, expressive self. We’ve seen this everywhere from street style in Paris to some of our favorite looks at the 2026 ESSENCE Festival of Culture. It makes sense that snakeskin bags are coming back into focus, too.

We’ve seen them everywhere, from Lupita Nyong'o carrying Brahmin on the Odyssey press tour to Khaite’s runway show in New York. Whether in a natural hue or a brighter, more artificial colorway, snake print adds something bold to any look, whether you’re headed to brunch or carrying it as your daily work bag. As Karefa-Johnson, who’s Depop’s Trend Spokesperson, says, “what I think is actually happening is people are just wanting to be loud and a bit messy again. Snakeskin gives you texture and a bit of wildness without committing to anything too extra.”

It helps that there’s been a crocodile bag wave since the spring, in large part to Chanel Creative Director Matthieu Blazy’s “Chanelmania” that descended when his debut collection hit store shelves. One of its stars? The reptilian-touched tote bags that went viral. (Karefa-Johnson herself bought the minty “mock-croc” shopping tote.) “Once something like that bag becomes the whole industry's obsession, everyone starts noticing animal prints and textures again, even outside of Chanel entirely,” the stylist, who’s worked with everyone from Bella Hadid to Vice President Kamala Harris, tells Refinery29.

If wearing snakeskin feels new or daring, style it as if it’s a neutral. As Karefa-Johnson says, “snakeskin actually plays really well with denim, T-shirts, and simple shapes because its texture is already doing a lot of work. Your outfit doesn't need to compete with it.” 

For anyone looking to score genuine snakeskin handbags without sticker shock, she shouts out Depop. “[It’s] a great place to source true vintage. You can find real snakeskin from the ’90s and early 2000s, which hit different than a lot of what's being made new right now. The leather is usually better, and it’s often available at a more affordable price point,” the stylist adds.

Ahead, we’ve rounded up our 11 favorite snakeskin bags o satisfy your craving and carry all summer long. The best part? There’s a range of styles and price points, with plenty that’ll work year-round and others that’ll be a star in your summer wardrobe.

title: The Official Summer Uniform Is Fun Pants & Basic Tops
text:
The Official Summer Uniform Is Fun Pants & Basic Tops

Forget simple jeans and “going-out tops”. Funky pants and basic tops might just be this summer’s chicest fashion formula.

Sometimes getting dressed is all about finding the right fashion formula. Every season brings a new trend, and this summer, it all comes down to funky pants. All summer, I couldn’t stop thinking about owning a pair of blue, yellow, and white striped pants. I wasn’t looking for a specific brand. I had simply imagined how good they would look with a tank top. That’s when I realized that I might have found this season’s ultimate outfit formula.

The thing about fashion is that it can make you crave something you never knew you wanted. And sometimes, that one unexpected piece ends up reflecting more about your own style than anything already hanging in your closet. 

Long before fun pants took over this season, there was sleepwear-inspired dressing. Over time, the pajama pants trend evolved into the colorful, expressive styles that we’re seeing today, in which bold prints, vibrant colors, playful silhouettes, and unexpected textures take center stage. Dolce & Gabbana’s Spring/Summer 2026 collection featured blue striped pajama-inspired trousers with embellishmed details, while Versace‘s Spring/Summer 2026 drop embraced bold blue, yellow, and orange striped pants with an ’80s-inspired feeling. And then suddenly, statement pants were not just for the bedroom, the beach, or the runways anymore. 

Live, Laugh, Love Fun Pants!

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Millie Bobby Brown (@milliebobbybrown)

This summer, statement pants are paired with the most understated tops, proving that sometimes one great piece is enough. A tank top, a baby tee, an oversized button-down shirt, or a bodysuit is all you need for styling, as inspired by Millie Bobby Brown, who paired Pamela Anderson’s archival embellished jeans with a fitted white baby tee, or Hailey Bieber, who paired bold polka-dot capris with a black boatneck top.

Celebrity and editorial stylist Lauren Croft told IMAGE that she’s “really drawn to those one-off eccentric pieces that are something different, and wearing that one statement piece that sets the tone for the whole outfit.” That’s exactly the role that fun pants have taken on this season. They will do all of the talking and can be the one unchangeable part of your style equation.

The best part? There are no rules. Animal print, sheer fabrics, embroidery, studs, bold colors, stripes, sequins, balloon silhouettes, barrel legs, or pajama-inspired styles all unite under the fun-pants umbrella. The only requirement is to have fun with them.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Leandra Medine Cohen (@leandramcohen)

During the day, style statement pants with a simple white crew-neck baby tee, flip-flops or ballet flats for coffee dates, lunch in the city, or summer vacations. When the sun goes down, you can switch the tee for a black satin strappy backless blouse, swap your flats for sleek heels or mules, layer on chunky jewelry, and the very same pants are instantly ready for dinner, rooftop drinks, or a summer party. For more styling inspiration, we can channel our inner Zara Larsson with bold-print trousers, a rhinestone bikini top or tied button-down shirt, and nostalgic accessories like statement sunglasses, skinny belts, and metallic kitten heels.

Personally, I’ve been reaching for my Lioness Penny Pants all summer long. The button-front detail running from the waist to the hem gives them (and me) plenty of personality. The simplicity of a basic top and minimalist jewelry let the pants shine. I’m also a fan of trousers long enough to cover my stilettos. They instantly make the silhouette feel sleeker, cooler, and bolder. 

So if you’re looking to refresh your wardrobe this summer, start with the pants, especially the funky ones.

title: This Pedicure Is Controversial, But I Wear It Every Spring & Summer
text:
This Pedicure Is Controversial, But I Wear It Every Spring & Summer

I’ve always loved a French pedicure. No matter what’s going on in my life, it always makes me feel polished, like I have my life together — even when I’m not wearing a lick of makeup, or I haven’t washed my hair in days. 

With that in mind, I’m thrilled that the design is making a comeback. But it’s not in the Y2K way you might remember from your teenage years (alongside velour tracksuits and frosted lip gloss). If Instagram is anything to go by, the French pedicure is chic and modern.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Harriet Westmoreland (@harrietwestmoreland)

What is a French pedicure? 

If you’re looking for a do-it-all pedicure that goes with everything and works for any occasion, the classic French is versatile. Whether you’re heading to the beach, the office, or your third wedding of the summer, it just works. Whether you love it or hate it, a French pedicure is a classic for a reason: “It’s clean, elegant, and endlessly wearable,” says Juanita Huber-Millet, founder and creative director of Townhouse. “Traditionally, this look features a soft nude or pink base with a crisp white tip.” Adding, “It’s that timeless contrast that makes it so instantly loved and recognizable.”

It’s little wonder, then, that the design is often spotted on some of the world’s biggest celebrities at red carpet events. Think Rihanna, Kylie Jenner, and Lily Allen, who are just a few stars frequently photographed with a fresh French pedicure. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Milly Mason (@millymason_)

What are the benefits of a French pedicure?

French pedicures aren’t limited to just pink and white; there are endless possibilities to explore with colors and creative designs: “French pedicures are back but in a unique and modern way,” says Fatima Naveed, senior brand manager at Duck & Dry. “We’re enjoying using fresh new shades and details to breathe new life into the traditional design,” like chrome and pastel tips, and jelly base colors.

Huber-Millet loves that the French pedicure complements every skin tone — and grows out beautifully. “It’s understated luxury that never goes out of style,” she says.

Why is the French pedicure considered controversial? 

But not everyone is sold on the French pedicure. If social media is anything to go by, it’s even a little controversial at times. Why? Naveed explains that the trend essentially emphasizes the overgrown tips of toenails, making critics question the look’s practicality. “Personally, though, I think that the key lies in the length as well as the choice of tip and base color,” she says. “A milky white or a sheer pink tip will give a more subtle, chic finish than bold white tips.” As for the base shade? “It’s more than just a background color; it sets the entire tone of the design.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Milly Mason (@millymason_)

What does the French pedicure look like in 2025? 

If you want to avoid the overgrown look, consider one of the biggest French pedicure trends. Enter: micro tips. “The micro French pedicure is gaining huge popularity,” says Naveed. “It consists of a very thin tip along the edge of toenails, which provides a clean and understated look.” The secret to pulling it off is keeping toenails short and well-groomed. This helps enhance the minimalist effect. Naveed’s clients also opt for a ‘Frombré’ effect (French ombré), which blends the nude base and milky white tip shades to lend a subtle, modern take on the look.

Huber-Millet adds that 2025 is seeing a real evolution of the French pedicure: “It’s all about tonal or unexpected color pairings, and playful accents like chrome, shimmer, or deep red shades for a moodier take. It’s fresh, flattering, and very now.”

title: 12 Fresh Bob Haircut Trends We’re Seeing Everywhere This Summer
text:
12 Fresh Bob Haircut Trends We’re Seeing Everywhere This Summer

When it comes to haircut trends, the choice is overwhelming, but if we had to crown one cut the current style du jour, it would be the bob. 

Its versatility is what gives the bob an edge over other cuts. Want to go really short? Consider the bixie, aka bob-meets-pixie. Worried about losing too much length? Try the lob, or long bob. That’s just the tip of the iceberg, because hairstylists from London to Los Angeles are dreaming up new iterations of the cut daily — and we predict that, this summer, there’ll be no escaping the temptation to brave the scissors.

With that in mind, scroll ahead for the bob haircut trends top stylists predict will reign supreme this summer and beyond.

DashDividers_1_500x100

The Korean Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Timothy Ting (@timothyting_hove)

Hairstylist George Curran bills the Korean bob as one of the most exciting haircut innovations. “The cut is designed so you can have a bob when your hair is tied or clipped up, and long hair when it’s worn down,” says Curren. It’s literally two hairstyles in one. “No extensions and all without committing to losing your length,” adds Curran. “It’s a clever optical illusion haircut using a specialist Korean cutting technique, and it’s perfect for anyone who wants versatility without compromise.” This video posted to Instagram by Timothy Ting is mesmerizing.

The Airy Bixie

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Jordz (@boyjordz.hair)

“This blends charm and delicacy with a modern and lived-in edge,” says Devin Graciano is a professional hairstylist and CEO of Goldie Locks. She adds, “The style is lightweight, soft, and full of movement, which gives it that effortless, airy feel,” — but it boasts attitude and intention, too. “The bixie complements the playful and confident person who wears it,” says Graciano. “It’s a cut that feels both current and timeless, with room for personalization depending on texture and personality.” This cut by Jordz is perfect. 

The Blunt Curly Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Nadine Koca | Fashion & Hair (@nadinekoca)

Curly hair specialist Dusty Schlabach predicts that the blunt curly bob will be everywhere. “It’s a zero-layer, ultra-clean blunt bob that sits right at the chin,” says Schlabach, adding, “It’s perfect for medium to low-density curls because it keeps the shape sleek without stacking or creating that Christmas tree effect at the baseline” — no triangular shapes here. Instead, the silhouette is “intentional,” says Schlabach, who suggests asking your stylist to cut your curls dry, exactly in their natural pattern. “Think a straight-across blunt line and no layers — just the slightest, almost invisible A-line so it sits clean at the chin,” says Schlabach. This cut on Nadine Koca is beautiful.

The Shattered Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Pam Mlunjwana (@pammacb)

Rather than a clean, blunt line, the ends of the shattered bob are point-cut or “shattered” by slicing into the hair vertically to create a “choppy, airy, slightly fragmented finish,” says Curran, like this look on Pam Mlunjwana. “It has that effortless, undone vibe,” he continues. But make no mistake: “It’s a very technical cut that relies on precision and the right styling products.” Layering is essential to add movement, says Curran. “You want the hair to have body and flow, without slipping into that helmet-like shape. I remove a lot of weight through the layers, particularly around the [back], which gives the cut bounce and stops it feeling heavy or bulky.”

Curran says the shattered bob looks best when it’s relaxed and a little tousled. “That cool-girl, lived-in texture feels intentional but never overdone. A product like Tecni Art Pli works really well, and finishing with Techni Art Volume Dust.”

The Bangless French Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Faick Zekai (@faick_hair)

When Curran thinks of a French bob, the words classic, timeless, and iconic spring to his mind. “In 2025, we saw this style evolve with softer layering around the face,” he says. “But as we head into 2026, it’s all about a more grown-out, effortless version of the look,” like this one by Faick Zekai. According to Curran, it stays sophisticated thanks to a strong, heavy finish through the ends and very minimal layering throughout.

The Liquid Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by TAMPA HAIRSTYLIST (@sophie.coastalhair)

Coined by Graciano, the liquid bob is a “sleek, softly sculpted bob with seamless layers and polished ends that move like fluid.” It’s glossy, weightless, and intentionally refined, she adds. Simply ask your stylist for a “blunt-to-soft perimeter bob,” advises Graciano, complete with subtle internal layering. “Wearing it blow-dried smooth emphasizes shine and swing,” says Graciano. This cut by Tampa hairstylist Sophie is stunning.

The Rounded Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Yasmeen ياسمين (@yasmeenscott)

According to Schlabach, the rounded layered curly bob — as seen here on Yasmeen Scott — is the total opposite of the aforementioned blunt bob. “This cut uses soft, intentional layers to create a rounder, more lifted shape that distributes weight evenly,” says Schlabach. “It’s ideal for dense curls that tend to build bulk at the bottom because the layers prevent heaviness and open up movement throughout the shape.”

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ashlynn Rudzinski (@arud_)

It looks just as great on straight and wavy hair, as shown by Ashlynn Rudzinski here. So what should you ask for? “A rounded bob with intentional layering to release weight and build shape — cut dry so the layers match the natural curl pattern and keep the silhouette lifted,” says Schlabach.

The Cowgirl Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by miho mai / 福岡ボブ / ボブ / ボブパーマ / 福岡美容室 / ナチュラル (@zoey__mai)

The cowgirl bob has a strong ’90s influence, says Curran. “I think it’s going to be a big evolution from the French bob or the blunt, one-length, ultra-polished look à la Sofia Richie-Grainge,” he adds. The cowgirl bob has a few defining attributes: “It’s softer, shaggier, and more relaxed — for those who don’t want a super-sleek finish and prefer a bit more movement and natural texture.” Curran points to Alexa Chung as inspiration. “What I love most is how bespoke you can make it,” adds Curran. “You can tailor it completely to the client and frame the face with soft or grown-out bangs.”

To style it, Curran recommends using a curling iron to create a subtle kick through the ends. “This will enhance that relaxed, cowgirl-inspired movement,” he says. “I always finish with L’Oréal Professionnel Tecni Art Volume Panache to keep the texture airy and full of body. You want it to look deliberately imperfect.” Miho Mai gets it so right here.

The Soft Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Faick Zekai (@faick_hair)

This is a rounded, gently layered bob, which Graciano says is designed to enhance natural texture. “It keeps the shape airy and controlled, never bulky,” she says — just like this cut by Faick Zekai. “Ask your stylist for a bob that hits between the jaw and collarbone, with light internal layering and curl-by-curl shaping to maintain softness and movement.”

The Asymmetric Pixie Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Sheridan Holyoak (@shmoakin_hair)

Brace yourselves: the pob, aka the pixie bob, is making a comeback — and Curran predicts it’ll be one of the standout cuts of 2026. “Think Scarlett Johansson circa 2015 or Victoria Beckham in her 2007 Posh bob era,” says Curran. He adds, “We’re seeing a real shift towards shapes that feel more architectural yet still wearable, and this cut ticks every box. I love the contrast it creates: one side sharp and cropped, the other slightly longer, sweeping, and sculpted.” Even better, Curran says it’s the ideal next step for anyone with a ’90s bob who wants to go shorter. “It’s bold, low-maintenance, and super stylish.” We adore this cut by Sheridan Holyoak. 

The Curly Lob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Jessenia Robayo (@jesseniaspallet)

Schlabach says that the curly lob, or long bob, is a slightly longer version of the rounded and blunt curly bobs. “It’s a shoulder-grazing cut that keeps length while maintaining structure,” adds Schlabach, “and it’s often paired with thoughtful face-framing or a soft veil bang to open up the front and create natural movement.” Thanks to the additional few inches, this style works well across most curl types and densities, says Schlabach. Remember to request some movement around the face to give it dimension, like this cut by Jessenia Robayo.

The Layered Bob

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by miho mai / 福岡ボブ / ボブ / ボブパーマ / 福岡美容室 / ナチュラル (@zoey__mai)

Curran says the layered bob was one of the most-liked bob haircuts on TikTok last month. “It’s a longer, ’90s-inspired style with layers at the front and throughout,” much like this cut by Miho Mai. The slightly wet-look texture emphasizes the choppiness of the layers, giving it a modern feel, while the lash-grazing full fringe brings in a touch of retro balance.
